summary: Kennard Lipman worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral studies under Herbert V. Guenther (attested 1979) and served as a sessional instructor at the University of Calgary.

Kenneth Ballhatchet (1922–1995) was an Indian history and Indology scholar. Educated at Clifton College and Peterhouse, Cambridge, he served as a Lecturer in the History of Modern India at SOAS (1948–1988) and Reader in Indian History at Oxford (1963–1965).
Kenneth Doo Young Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Ryuichi Abe and held a post at Stetson University (attested 2007).

Kenneth G. Zysk is an Indology and history scholar. He studied at UC Santa Barbara and Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, later holding posts at Eastern Michigan University, UCLA, and the University of Copenhagen.

Kenneth J. Guest is a scholar of religious studies and Sinology. He studied at Columbia, Peking University, Union Theological Seminary, and the CUNY Graduate Center, also studying under Aloysius Pieris, and held positions at Hunter College and Baruch College.

Kenneth J. Saunders (1883–1937) was a religious and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Emmanuel College and under W. D. C. Wagiswara, he served at Trinity College, Hartford, YMCA College, Pacific School of Religion, and the University of California.

Kenneth K. Inada (1923–2011) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as a philosophy professor at the University at Buffalo and chaired both the Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai (until 1999) and the Numata Center (1996–1999).

Kenneth K. S. Ch'en (1907–1986) was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi, Yenching, and Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, later holding professorships at Harvard, UCLA, and Princeton.

Kenneth K. Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Stanford, the Institute of Buddhist Studies, Eastern Institute, University of Tokyo, and UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini. He held faculty posts at Berkeley, IBS, and Musashino University.
Kenneth R. Valpey is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He was educated at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and held a post at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Kenneth Somerled Macdonald (1832–1903) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. Educated at the University of Aberdeen and New College, Edinburgh, he worked with the United Free Church Mission (~1862–1903) and was a fellow at the University of Calcutta.

Kenneth W. Jones (1934–1996) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Stockton University and UC Berkeley under Thomas Metcalf, he taught at Kansas State University from 1965, becoming a Distinguished Professor in 1989.

Kenryo Minowa is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorates at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Aichi Gakuin University, the University of Tokyo, and Rissho University, and chaired the Japanese Association of Indian and Buddhist Studies.
Kenryu Nishio is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He received his doctorate from Otani University and became a professor emeritus at Hanazono University.
Kenryu Tsuji (1919–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his studies at Ryukoku University (1938) and the University of Toronto.

Kenryu Tsukinowa (1888–1969) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar educated at Bukkyo University. He founded the Society of Tantric Buddhism (1960) and held professorships at Koyasan, Seizan, Shuchiin, and Ryukoku universities.
Kenshi Kusano is a scholar in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Otani University (~1971–1980) and later became a professor there (~2000).
Kenta Suzuki is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo, and he held an associate professorship at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College (~2014).

Kenyu Mitomo is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. Educated at Rissho University and UC Berkeley, he served as Dean of Buddhist Studies at Rissho University (1968–2015) and held visiting roles at Berkeley, Chung-Hwa Institute, and Otani University.

Kevin A. Vose is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed degrees at Bates College and the University of Virginia, studying under traditional teacher Khen Rinpoche Ngawang Jinpa and doctoral supervisor Jeffrey Hopkins.
